% note: Stamped note of free analysis 1, in its own words: ``$d$ \ensuremath{>}~0 means one Haiku-max try scored higher than the lower-effort vote at the same money. Each row is within one study and one set; the two studies are never pooled. Under the 1/$m$ tie rule a 2-try vote scores about its single try.''
% note: Stamped note of free analysis 7, in its own words: ``Exploratory arm, post hoc interval; $d$ \ensuremath{>}~0 means the Haiku-max try scored higher.''
% note: In those two stamped notes, a ``try'' is a sample, an ``arm'' is a setting and ``at the same money'' is cost-matched.
% note: Samples per Haiku-max sample: one Haiku-max sample's list cost divided by the list cost of one sample of the setting in the row. Cost-matched: the vote's $k$ is the floor of the samples per Haiku-max sample, held to the setting's designed samples, so the vote costs no more than one Haiku-max sample. Study~1 costs are in US dollars per puzzle and Study~1b costs in US dollars per answer, as each study stamps them.
% note: On pieces (6\ensuremath{\times}1) the chains' cost-matched vote, $k$~=~4, costs more than one Haiku-max sample (cost column), so it is shown without a paired interval; the cost-matched vote on this shape has $k$~=~3.
% note: Format compliance (pre-specified descriptive) is that of the setting's own samples; a vote is taken over the same samples. Haiku-max was an exploratory setting in Study~1.
% note: No row is a test: the paired differences carry no $p$-value, no Holm correction and no verdict. Each row stays within one study.
